meta.notes: Instructions so correct they rearrange other people's work. Carried Mae's box in February and ordered its slip. Praise so conditional it reveals the trap. Hears the Wills pun and writes "See me."

threads.source: B05. Alive. Her corrections as a form of affection.

threads.topic: The register at the shop. You'd know that hand?
threads.source: Comic hurt. The player cannot correct a dead woman's sevens, because the player is the dead woman.

threads.topic: Mr. Wren was at your door with a paper.
Mr. Wren says you have his drafts.
threads.source: Suspect chain, Peter. The same comedy, after. She dates everything she marks.

threads.topic: They say you were received, Mrs. Marsh.

em_s1.line: I carried Mrs. Kessler's box across for her certificates, as she does not lift. Miss Voss is a capable woman whose seven is open at the top. Someone will read it as a nine. I told her so. She has since begun doing it on purpose, which I take as attention.

em_s2.line: A ledger, and I am not in the habit. The slip is mine: "One box, Mrs. K., to go back the same day." I put it square on the table. Miss Voss moved it. I moved it back. It's a very good table for that.

em_s3.line: She is improving. That is the highest thing I say about anyone, and I said it once about a boy who became a bishop and I have regretted it since.

em_a1.line: "Mrs. K., certificate plates, Mon. 4 Feb." Yes. There's the seven, in the fourth line, still open at the top. I gave her that note in February. I find I have not forgiven it. One ought to be allowed to finish marking.

choices.label: Then why did you keep the slip?

em_a2.line: I beg your pardon? You are the maintenance. You have an opinion of Miss Voss's numerals? ... Well. So had she. It's the same opinion, and it was wrong then. See me if you wish to improve.

em_a3.line: A slip is kept until the thing is returned. It came back the same day, by another hand, and nobody signed for it. I do not like an open slip. I have been told this is the whole of my character, and by whom you'd be surprised.

em_d1.line: A memorandum, and he brought it to me as if I had set it. He has come to me about commas since he was eleven. It is dated, because I date what I mark. It is not yet good. It is not yet anything. I have told him so in red.

em_da1.line: Seven, dated, the first on the eighth of June. The grammar was mine to correct and the first of August was not. The fourth draft was good enough. I marked it anyway.

choices.label: If you had passed the fourth?

em_da2.line: I beg your pardon? He would have sent it in June. I am aware of the date. See me if you wish to improve.

em_o1.line: I stood in her shop and counted them out with her. She reached two and tied the bag. I have written "twelve" on a card and left it on her counter. She thanked me. That is the worst thing about it.

em_o2.line: So I am told. I have kept a programme log for eleven years and I know precisely where I stopped. Well?

em_o3.line: You will not. I sleep perfectly well at two, thank you.

em_p1.line: The seating was a disgrace. I moved three of them. Nobody remarked on it. I moved them back, to see, and nobody remarked on that. I have taught children who would not look at me, and I know how it is done, and it was done well.
